candidates.title: Referee verifier for audit/prt2 cannot be built from audited source: regenerated UArchStep.sol references undeclared TLB_NUM_SETS
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 regenerated from audit/prt2 (UArchStep.sol / EmulatorConstants.sol), root cause src/uarch-step.cpp of the emulator
candidates.role: Referee verifier (AUDIT.md: 'machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1, with its generated code and constants regenerated from audit/prt2 | Referee verifier'); the source is the emulator's uarch-step.cpp (honest-operator role)
candidates.location: src/uarch-step.cpp:890 (executeECALL, `if (set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS || slot_index >= TLB_SET_SIZE)`, added by commit afd5f9d); TLB_NUM_SETS is an enumerator of src/shadow-tlb.hpp:34. Generator side: work/solidity-step/released/helper_scripts/generate_UArchStep.sh (qualifies only identifiers found in src/EmulatorConstants.sol), helper_scripts/generate_EmulatorConstants.lua (does not emit TLB_NUM_SETS), templates/EmulatorConstants.sol.template (defines only TLB_SLOT_LENGTH, TLB_SET_SIZE, TLB_SET_LENGTH). Result: work/solidity-step/regenerated/src/UArchStep.sol:1090 `set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS` (unqualified) next to `EmulatorConstants.TLB_SET_SIZE`.
candidates.description: Commit afd5f9d added a TLB set-index check to the shared uarch step (uarch-step.cpp) and states 'UArchStep.sol picks up the check when it is regenerated'. It does not: the pinned machine-solidity-step generator translates uarch-step.cpp textually and prefixes `EmulatorConstants.` only to names that EmulatorConstants.sol defines; TLB_NUM_SETS is neither generated by generate_EmulatorConstants.lua nor present in the template, so the pure regeneration from audit/prt2 produces UArchStep.sol that fails to compile (solc Error 7576 'Undeclared identifier'). There is therefore no way to obtain the on-chain verifier of this emulator version from audited source with the pinned tools: the harness had to add a hand-written line `uint64 constant TLB_NUM_SETS = 3;` (bugs/harness/solidity-step/patches/01-tlb-num-sets.sh) to a template, and Dave was built on that hand-patched variant. Any deployer hits the same failure and must hand-edit the verifier (choosing a value, or deleting the check, or keeping the released v0.17.0-test1 UArchStep.sol that lacks the check), i.e. ship verifier code that does not come from audited source.
candidates.trigger: Whoever builds the deployment's verifier for this emulator version (deployer, auditor, or an honest operator checking the deployed bytecode) runs the documented regeneration (make generate-step generate-reset generate-send-cmio-response generate-constants against audit/prt2) and forge build.
candidates.reachability: Deterministic on every regeneration from audit/prt2 HEAD (and from every commit since afd5f9d). Not state dependent.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No. The trigger is the build of the verifier from the emulator source and the pinned generator, not a deployment violating A1-A8; and R13 itself puts the obligation on the code: 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source.' The exclusion 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8' does not apply because the emulator's own source is what makes A6 ('Every verifier, the uarch program fixed on-chain, and every honest operator in a deployment implements the same state transition function (R13)') impossible to meet from audited source. 2 Role: referee verifier (regenerated machine-solidity-step, AUDIT.md table); root cause in the emulator's uarch-step.cpp, which every implementation shares. 3 High/Medium cases: matches the High case 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source.' Here it cannot be built at all from audited source. 4 Alternative reading: if the deployed verifier necessarily diverges from audited source (any deployment must hand-edit it), the qualifier 'while what is deployed matches its audited source' fails and step 4 applies: R13's build obligation is violated for every deployment of this version, rated Critical. Facts that decide: whether a deployment of this version must ship hand-edited code (yes, with the pinned generator) and what the hand edit is (the harness value 3 is correct; deleting the check reproduces the pre-afd5f9d verifier, which accepts a WRITE_TLB at a wrapped address, a High R3 issue from unreachable states). 5 n/a. Claimed: High (Critical under the second reading).
candidates.threat_to_goal: The goal relies on A6 (one STF across the uarch, the verifiers and the operator). The verifier of this version is not derivable from audited source, so the referee's ground truth becomes whatever hand edit the deployer makes; a wrong edit (another TLB_NUM_SETS value, removing the check, or reusing the released UArchStep.sol) yields a verifier that differs from the emulator's uarch-step and from the operator, and nobody can check the deployed bytecode against audited source.
candidates.evidence: Harness logs (not re-run, they are deterministic): bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/build-status.txt and build.log: 'pure regeneration: forge build FAILED: Error (7576): Undeclared identifier. --> src/UArchStep.sol:1090:30: set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS'. grep shows TLB_NUM_SETS absent from released/templates, released/helper_scripts and released/src; generate_UArchStep.sh builds the qualification list from `grep constant src/EmulatorConstants.sol`. Commit afd5f9d message: 'UArchStep.sol picks up the check when it is regenerated.' The patched variant (with the hand-added constant) then passes test-replay 56/56.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: copy work/solidity-step/released to a temp dir, run its generate-step/generate-constants (EMULATOR_DIR shim to this repo, constants from the in-tree Lua module as the harness does) and `forge build`; exit 1 if the build fails, 0 if it succeeds. A cheaper deterministic proxy: list every upper-case identifier used in src/uarch-step.cpp that is not defined in uarch-step.cpp/.hpp or EmulatorCompat, and require each to appear in the generated EmulatorConstants.sol; fails today on TLB_NUM_SETS.

candidates.title: PRT player checks only the pristine uarch hash and factory geometry, never CM_MARCHID, so it accepts deployments of another version whose verifier differs outside the uarch image
candidates.component: doc/recipes/crisium.lua (PRT player start-up), doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua read_geometry, doc/recipes/prt-deploy.lua
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'), standing in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua:127-134 (only `UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH()` of the factory's stateTransition is compared with cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH, then bridge.read_geometry); prt-bridge.lua:873-892 (read_geometry compares tournament heights with the emulator's rollup constants); prt-deploy.lua:43-47 (same pristine-only check). The deployed CartesiStateTransition publishes `CM_MARCHID` for exactly this purpose (dave/released prt/contracts/src/state-transition/CartesiStateTransition.sol:35-44: 'published so a claimer can compare it with its own emulator before joining, as with CM_MARCHID'); no recipe reads it (grep CM_MARCHID doc/recipes: no hit).
candidates.description: R13 requires the honest operator to 'detect and refuse a mismatch between its build and a deployment' and 'The check must refuse every pairing of its build with a deployment of another released version.' The player's only build-versus-deployment checks are the pristine uarch state hash and the tournament geometry. The pristine hash covers only the uarch RAM image and initial registers. Large parts of the STF that R13 lists live outside it: the uarch instruction semantics and the 'accesses each logged transition makes, and their order' (UArchStep.sol, from src/uarch-step.cpp), the uarch reset (UArchReset.sol), input delivery (SendCmioResponse.sol: revert root, imcyclemax) and the position-to-form map plus rollup constants inside CartesiStateTransition (LOG2_INPUT_WINDOW_SPAN, UARCH_CYCLE_MASK, internal constants the player cannot read). This branch's own history shows such changes: 4310fa3 ('Root hashes are unchanged, but a logged step at the cycle limit now also reads the halt flag, so the Solidity step must be regenerated') and afd5f9d (new TLB check in uarch-step.cpp) change only host-side uarch-step code, not the uarch image. A deployment whose verifier was generated from a version differing only there has the same pristine hash; the player accepts it and plays, and its uarch-level proofs at the affected positions can be rejected (completeness failure) or the dispute settles on a different STF. Comparing CM_MARCHID with cartesi.MARCHID is the check the deployment offers and the player omits it. (Aggravation: CM_MARCHID alone is also ambiguous across released versions, since v0.22.0 and the v0.23.0-test1/test2 tags carry marchid 22 while mimpid differs, see candidate 4; the deployment does not publish mimpid.)
candidates.trigger: A deployment (honest deployer error or a version upgrade on one side) pairs the operator's emulator build with a CartesiStateTransition generated from another emulator version whose uarch image is identical; the honest player starts against it.
candidates.reachability: Reachable whenever two emulator versions share the uarch image but differ in uarch-step.cpp/uarch-reset/send-cmio-response or rollup constants; the branch history contains such a pair of trees (parent of 4310fa3 vs 4310fa3, both marchid 22). Detection never depends on guest state.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The mismatch itself is a deployment violating A6, which is excluded for the emulator, but R13 makes detecting and refusing it an obligation of the honest operator, so the defect is the missing refusal, not the mismatch. 2 Role: support (player/bridge per AUDIT.md), standing in for the honest operator; per section 3 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. 3 In the honest-operator role it matches the High case 'A node that cannot detect a version mismatch, while every node in fact runs the deployment's version' (and Critical by step 4 when a mismatch is actually present, R13 / A6 on the honest operator's path). Capped for support: Medium. 4/5 n/a.
candidates.threat_to_goal: If the operator does not refuse a deployment of another version, it plays a dispute whose referee implements a different STF: its leaf proofs at positions where the two STFs differ (cycle-limit halts, logged accesses, delivery) fail on-chain, the honest claim is eliminated, and a dishonest claim can win (completeness failure, section 1).
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: crisium.lua:127-134 and prt-deploy.lua:43-47 compare UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH only; no CM_MARCHID read anywhere in doc/recipes; CartesiStateTransition publishes CM_MARCHID with a comment saying claimers should compare it. git show 4310fa3 / afd5f9d: host-side uarch-step changes only.
candidates.test_idea: Local chain harness: deploy the released Dave stack, but make the factory's stateTransition a contract (e.g. a thin Solidity mock, or CartesiStateTransition built against an EmulatorConstants with CM_MARCHID = cartesi.MARCHID - 1 and the same pristine hash). Start crisium.lua in sentinel mode with that application; the test requires that start-up fails with a version-mismatch error before the first epoch. Today it proceeds (exit 1).

candidates.title: Machine-identification registers cannot tell released pre-release versions apart: marchid is bumped once per cycle, mimpid encodes only major.minor, the label is encoded nowhere
candidates.component: src/Makefile (EMULATOR_MARCHID, EMULATOR_VERSION_*), tools/template/cm-version.h.template / src/cm-version.h (CM_MIMPID = major*1000+minor), src/machine.cpp validate_processor_shadow
candidates.location: src/cm-version.h:20,35; src/Makefile:17-23; src/machine.cpp:205-217; history: git log -L17,23:src/Makefile shows the tree labelled 0.23.0-test2 carried EMULATOR_MARCHID=22 (as v0.22.0) until 6e3e4d3 'chore!: bump MARCHID to 23' (2026-11-13), after STF-changing commits (4310fa3, afd5f9d, a857edf, 75e9f89, de2a679, 2175acb, 0dfebe1).
candidates.description: R13: 'Every version that changes the state transition function changes the machine-identification registers in the hashed state.' The registers are mvendorid (constant), marchid (bumped by hand, once per release cycle) and mimpid = major*1000+minor (no patch, no label). Released tags exist for v0.22.0-test1/-test2/-test3, v0.22.0, v0.23.0-test1 and v0.23.0-test2 (git ls-remote). On this branch the tree labelled 0.23.0-test2 had marchid 22 and mimpid 23, so the released v0.23.0-test1 and v0.23.0-test2 almost certainly share all three registers (marchid 22, mimpid 23), and v0.22.0-test1..3 and v0.22.0 share (22, 22). If any of those consecutive releases changed the STF (the cycle's commits are mostly STF fixes, and this branch shows commits that do, e.g. 4310fa3 'fix!' at marchid 22), the emulator's load/create check (validate_processor_shadow) accepts a template or stored machine of the other release, and the on-chain CM_MARCHID cannot distinguish their verifiers. The manual's claim that the registers are checked 'to ensure the configuration matches the running emulator version' then does not hold across those releases. Not verified blind: needs a comparison of STF sources and EMULATOR_MARCHID between the tags (outside this branch).
candidates.trigger: An honest operator running one released pre-release (e.g. v0.23.0-test2) adopts a template or deployment made with another (v0.23.0-test1, same registers) whose STF differs.
candidates.reachability: Depends on the tagged releases; this branch's HEAD itself (marchid 23) is distinguishable from all of them.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No exclusion covers the version-identification policy. 2 Role: honest operator (validate_processor_shadow on load/create, AUDIT.md 'storing, loading ... machines'). 3 If confirmed and the pristine hash still differs (so the player's pristine check catches it), the matching case is High 'A node that cannot detect a version mismatch, while every node in fact runs the deployment's version.' 4 If two such releases share registers and pristine hash, the honest operator cannot refuse the pairing at all: R13 violated on the honest operator's path, Critical. 5 If no consecutive released pair differs in STF, it is only a latent process gap (Low). Claimed High pending the tag comparison.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Version mixing (A6) is the one way a correct emulator still loses disputes; the registers are the in-state mechanism R13 relies on to refuse it, and they do not change between released versions of the same minor.
candidates.evidence: git log -L17,23:src/Makefile (4310fa3: EMULATOR_MARCHID=22 with VERSION 0.23.0-test2; 6e3e4d3 bumps to 23 and its message lists the STF changes of the cycle). `git ls-remote --tags` on the public emulator repository lists v0.22.0-test1..3, v0.22.0, v0.23.0-test1, v0.23.0-test2 (tag contents not read). Released machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 publishes CM_MARCHID 22.
candidates.test_idea: A prover allowed to read tags: for each consecutive pair of released tags with equal (marchid, mimpid), generate the step (or run tests/lua uarch logs) from both and compare UArchStep.sol/uarch-pristine-hash and a fixed set of step logs; exit 1 if any pair with equal registers has a different STF. In-branch: a test asserting CM_MIMPID changes with the label/patch (or marchid with every tag) would fail today.

candidates.title: Uarch toolchain not fully pinned: binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf floats, base image by mutable tag, packages from the live Debian archive
candidates.role: Honest operator / deployment build of the uarch program and its pristine hash
candidates.location: Dockerfile:1-17 (BUILD_BASE=debian:trixie-20250811 by tag, `apt-get update` against the live archive, only gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf=14.2.0+19 and g++-14-riscv64-linux-gnu=14.2.0-19cross1 pinned; binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, which assembles and links uarch-ram.elf and runs objcopy, is unpinned); uarch/Makefile (LD/OBJCOPY/OBJDUMP from the toolchain prefix, -lgcc from the gcc package).
candidates.description: R13 requires the uarch program and its pristine hash to be 'reproducibly buildable from audited source'. uarch-ram.bin (hence UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH) depends on the assembler, linker and objcopy of binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, whose version is whatever the archive serves at build time (today 2.44-3+7+b1 in trixie). The pinned compiler versions are fetched from deb.debian.org, not snapshot.debian.org, so once trixie publishes a newer gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf in a point release the pinned version disappears and the Dockerfile no longer builds; a binutils update could silently change linker relaxation/layout and so the pristine hash. Today the rebuild matches (harness uarch-rebuild: 0x89ae...43d7, uarch-ram.bin sha256 e776...eb54).
candidates.trigger: Anyone rebuilding the uarch from the Dockerfile after a Debian trixie update of binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf or gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf.
candidates.reachability: Not currently failing; depends on future archive changes (madison today: trixie gcc 14.2.0+19, binutils 2.44-3+7+b1).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Not out of scope. 2 Role: build of the uarch program fixed on-chain (honest operator / deployment). 3 The High case 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt' does not hold today (rebuild agrees). 4 No rule is violated at present. 5 Low (latent reproducibility gap); becomes High once the archive changes.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Loss of the ability to verify that the deployed pristine hash comes from audited source; does not by itself change any hash.
candidates.evidence: bugs/harness/work/uarch-rebuild/report.txt (all agree, binutils 2.44-3+7+b1 noted as unpinned); qa.debian.org madison output for gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf and binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf.
candidates.test_idea: A static check that every package used to build the uarch (gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf, binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, g++-14-riscv64-linux-gnu) is pinned to an exact version and the base image by digest or a snapshot.debian.org source; fails today on binutils and the base tag.
